entry.title: Meet Magnific Move: motion graphics you can talk to
entry.summary: A motion graphics editor you can talk to. Describe what you want, ask for changes in your own words, and download an MP4.
entry.content:
A motion graphics editor you can talk to. Describe what you want, ask for changes in your own words, and download an MP4.

Making motion graphics has always been slow - not because the ideas are hard, but because the tools are. You need the software, the skills and a few days for every version. So most teams make fewer than they need: a launch gets one video, and a social post gets a still image. Magnific Move changes that.

Move is an agent-based motion graphics editor. You describe what you want, an agent builds it, you ask for changes in your own words, and then you download an MP4. No timeline, no keyframes and no animation software.

Vibe motion

You've probably heard of vibe coding: you describe what you want, and AI writes the code. Move does the same for motion graphics. You say what you want, and the agent animates it.

This wasn't possible a year ago. The new AI models do more than generate pictures. They plan, write code, check their own work and fix it. And motion graphics are a perfect fit for that, because a motion graphic is really design plus timing, and both can be written as code.

The missing piece was a format agents can actually work in. HyperFrames, the open-source framework from HeyGen, laid that foundation. It lets an agent write a motion graphic as plain HTML, preview it, check it frame by frame and render it to MP4. That's what powers Move. Around it, Move adds everything you need as a person: the editor, the versions, your Brand Kit and the rest of Magnific.

What this means for you: because every motion is built as code, Move can change one element without touching the rest, save every edit as a new version, and let you go back or try a new direction at any time. You never touch the code. You just say what you want.

Describe it, then direct it

You start by writing what you need, or by picking a template. You choose the format, the length and your Brand Kit, and a few minutes later the agent has built a first version, with text, shapes, images, transitions, music and voiceover. One of the best parts is what happens when you're vague. Write "the end looks boring", and it doesn't guess. It asks which part you mean, with choices, the way a good motion designer would.

Then the real work starts, because the first version is never the one you ship. This is where Move is different from a video model: ask for a bigger title, and you get a bigger title, while everything else stays exactly the same. If it's easier to point than to explain, you pause the video, click the spot and leave a comment. Every edit becomes a new version, and nothing is ever overwritten, so you can branch off to try another idea, compare two versions side by side and go back whenever you want.

That's possible because a motion in Move is code, not pixels. When you ask for a change, the agent edits the code and renders it again, so nothing gets lost along the way. Text stays sharp, colors stay exact, and your 20th version looks as clean as the first. That's very different from how AI video usually works. There, every change means generating the clip again, and you hope the parts you liked survive.

It's also fast enough to keep going. An edit takes a minute or two, so working in Move feels more like a conversation than a render queue.

Your brand, your files, all of Magnific

Your Brand Kit takes care of colors, fonts and logo, so every motion looks like you. And Move isn't limited to text and shapes. It can use all the AI models on Magnific, and you just ask for what you need in your own words. Write "generate a close-up of the product on a dark background", or "add a short video of someone using it", and Move makes the images, video, music, sound effects and voiceover, and builds them into your motion. You can bring your own files too, like a product shot, a clip of yourself or your own track.

And when you need the same motion in another format, Move doesn't crop it. It recomposes every shot for 9:16, 1:1, 4:5 or whatever you need, and you export it as an MP4 in 1080p or 4K, up to 180 seconds.

One more thing you can try. Move is also a quick way to block out a 3D shot. Ask it to assemble a Lego house in 3D, and you get the layout, the timing and the camera move in a few minutes. Then take that video into Seedance 2.5 and make it look real.

No blank page

The easiest way in is a template, and there are lots of them, from launch films to logo reveals. Each one comes with its full prompt, so you can see how it was made. Open one, click Use template, and tell Move what to change.

Want a step-by-step guide? Read how to get started with Move in the Help Center.

Move is live today, under Motion graphics on Magnific. Make something and share it with #MagnificMove. We can't wait to see what you build with it.

Try Magnific Move

entry.title: Magnific One: Every AI image looks the same. Here's how we're fixing it.
entry.summary: Write a few words and get an image that looks art-directed and stays on brand. Here’s what Magnific One does, how people reacted in a blind test, and how to try it unlimited until October 15.
entry.content:
Write a few words and get an image that looks art-directed and stays on brand. Here’s what Magnific One does, how people reacted in a blind test, and how to try it unlimited until October 15.

Every AI image now looks like every other AI image. Same light. Same faces. Same posters.

We built Magnific One to fix that: an image model with art direction built in.

Here’s what it does, how people reacted in a blind test, how we launched it, and how to try it.

Magnific One does three things other image models don’t.

Aesthetics: every image looks directed

You write a few words. Magnific One adds what an art director would: the composition, the light, the camera angle.

That changes how you prompt. Short prompts work better than you’d think: some of our favorite images started with a single word, like “cinematic” or “documentary”. Say what matters, and let the model do the directing.

“Having something that feels like an Art Director guiding the creative process opens up so many possibilities.”
— Azed, creator

Draft mode: explore before you commit

Most of art direction is choosing. Draft gives you 8 or 16 different directions from one prompt, for the price of one image, so you can see your options before you commit. Pick the one you like and make it final, in 2K or 4K.

Brand Kit: your brand in every image

Set up your brand once, from your website, a PDF or a few images. Brand Kit captures your palette, type, imagery and tone, and every final image follows it, whoever on the team is generating.

The more it knows, the more it looks like you. Add a written guideline, up to 50 reference images, and simple rules like “logo bottom left”.

“Within a couple of hours of going back and forth with the agent, we were able to create such a breadth of content that’s all on brand and ready to go.”
— Rourke Heath, CEO and founder, GenHQ

In a blind test, people chose Magnific One

Before launch, we ran a blind test. Voters saw two images made from the same prompt by different models, without knowing which model made which, and picked the one they preferred. Five models took part: Magnific One, Midjourney, GPT Image 2, Nano Banana 2 and Seedream 5 Pro.

We opened it to creators, partners and business customers outside Magnific. Magnific One was the only model to win more than half of its matchups: people preferred its image almost two times out of three.

Or test it yourself. In the Image Generator, select Magnific One and the model you use today, run the same prompt, and compare.

Why we built it

AI images are easy to make. Hard to make right.

Our team has spent years learning what makes an image good. But there was no place to put that knowledge. And our users had thirty models and no way to choose. So we built the image model we wanted ourselves, made for the work marketing and brand teams do every day.

Launch night in Singapore

On October 8, I showed Magnific One for the first time, at our Upscale Day in Singapore. We had chosen an art gallery for it: the perfect setting to launch an image model with art direction built in. Every piece on the wall had been chosen, placed and lit by someone with taste. That’s art direction. That’s what Magnific One is about.

I’m usually a bit nervous before I go on stage. This time, I wasn’t. I was just excited. Excited to finally show the world what we’d built.

I finished my last slide. And then, applause.

Months of work, on the technology behind Magnific One and on the launch itself, came down to that moment. At 21:30 in Singapore, 15:30 in Madrid, Magnific One went live everywhere.

The first day

In the first 24 hours, thousands of people made images with Magnific One, and many of them set up their own Brand Kit.

We even made real cereal boxes for the night: Magnific One, "Art direction, built in", fortified with Brand Kit. People took them home.

“With my own characters and styles, it's really damn good!”
— Paige Piskin, creator

Plans and pricing

Magnific One is available on all paid plans, in 2K or 4K and in High or Max quality. You’ll find the current credits for each option on our Pricing page.

Try it, unlimited

Until October 15, Magnific One is unlimited in the Magnific desktop app for Premium+, Pro and Business.

We're creatives too. This one means a lot to us. Come see what it can do.

Try Magnific One

entry.title: How to Create an AI Short Film with Magnific: Out Loud
entry.summary: Learn how to create an AI short film with Magnific, from character design to cinematic sequences, using the Out Loud workflow and 22 prompts.
entry.content:
Learn how to create an AI short film with Magnific, from character design to cinematic sequences, using the Out Loud workflow and 22 prompts.

Creating an AI short film means making decisions that hold together across every scene: who the character is, how the world looks, what a performance communicates, and when to cut.

In Out Loud, we follow Luca from private bedroom rehearsals to a talent-show audition, where judgment begins before the first note. The story unfolds through small details: a hand tightening around a backpack, a nervous glance, a child repeating an adult’s reaction.

Here, we break down how the film was made with Magnific, from character design in Nano Banana Pro to video generation with Seedance 2.5 Draft. You’ll find 22 prompts covering character variations, locations, individual shots, and multishot sequences, along with practical guidance for adapting the workflow to your own film.

How to create an AI short film with Magnific

The workflow starts with a consistent set of visual references. Develop your character, establish the environments, and prepare recurring props before generating the scenes. Then direct the action shot by shot and bring the selected footage into your edit.

For Out Loud, the workflow combined:

  • Nano Banana Pro in Magnific for character and location images.
  • Magnific stock assets and Designer for the audition flyer.
  • Seedance 2.5 Draft in Magnific for video sequences, followed by conversion to HD.
  • Adobe After Effects for post-production.
  • Adobe Premiere Pro for editing.

Each stage serves a different creative decision. The images establish what belongs in the world. The video prompts direct what happens within it. The edit determines how those moments build into a story.

Before you use the prompts

The prompts below retain their original Spanish and English wording, with internal asset IDs replaced by readable reference names.

Attach your own reference images wherever a prompt calls for a character, location, or prop. A label such as @LUCA_CASA identifies a reference; typing the label alone will not supply the image.

Prepare these assets before generating:

  • Character references: one approved identity, plus the outfits needed for each scene.
  • Bedroom references: variations for daytime, nighttime, and different states of tidiness.
  • Audition references: the stage, judges, venue exterior, and waiting area.
  • Graphic props: a finished flyer, event sign, and calendar.

The collection includes alternate versions of some scenes. Use the version that fits your shot list, and adapt the durations to your sequence.

1. Create a consistent AI character with Nano Banana Pro

Start with the casting portrait. Luca’s design specifies hair, complexion, skin texture, expression, and lighting before introducing a setting or action. This gives the character a clear visual identity that can carry across the film.

Once you have an approved portrait, use it as a reference for the wardrobe variations. Check the face, haircut, and proportions each time. The audition outfit, pajamas, and everyday looks should all feel like the same person at different moments.

Neutral backgrounds keep the focus on those decisions. You can assess character continuity before adding the complexity of a bedroom, bus, or stage.

Prompt 1: Cast Luca

Director de casting cinematográfico, fondo de estudio neutro gris azulado, luz plana y fría con un ligero tono azul-verdoso (cool cinematic grade). Adolescente de 15 años, sin género definido, complexión gorda, piel pálida con textura realista (pecas y textura natural, sin retocar). Corte de pelo mullet ondulado y rubio por la parte interna de abajo, con flequillo recto y corto justo por encima de las cejas, pelo castaño oscuro con volumen natural, más corto arriba y en el flequillo, más largo y suelto por detrás y a los lados. Maquillaje sutil tipo delineado ligeramente corrido/ahumado, como si se lo hubiera hecho ella misma sin mucha técnica, labios naturales. Expresión seria mirando a cámara, fotografía de casting. Camiseta básica blanca.

Prompt 2: Create the audition outfit

viste a @img1con esta ropa **Prenda superior:** Chaqueta deportiva tipo track jacket, cuello alto con cremallera, color azul marino con panel de cuello y puños en rojo, franjas de rayas diagonales en tonos burdeos/rojo oscuro sobre los hombros y mangas (sin ningún logo, escudo ni texto — superficie lisa donde iría el emblema). Ajuste ligeramente oversize, cremallera subida hasta el cuello.
**Prenda inferior:** Falda larga plisada de cuadros escoceses (tartán) en tonos azul marino, gris y burdeos apagados, con vuelo amplio, largo midi hasta el tobillo.
**Calzado:** Zapatillas deportivas retro en blanco con detalles burdeos/granate (sin logo de marca visible), calcetines/medias oscuras cortas por debajo del tobillo.
**Accesorios:** Un colgante fino de cadena metálica dorada con un pequeño dije (forma libre, no reconocible/genérico), llevado por fuera de la chaqueta.
**Paleta de color general:** Azul marino, rojo/burdeos y gris — combinación deportiva retro con la falda de cuadros dando el contraste "colegial descuidado".

Prompt 3: Create the pajamas

viste a @img1 como **PIJAMA**
Director de casting cinematográfico, fondo de estudio neutro gris azulado, luz plana y fría. Misma Luca, mullet suelto y algo despeinado como recién levantada. De pie o en pose relajada, cuerpo entero, mirada directa a cámara, postura cómoda y sin poses. Viste camiseta de manga corta color crudo/beige claro con un pequeño gráfico decorativo desteñido en el pecho (diseño genérico, sin texto ni marca legible), combinada con short de chándal corto en azul (azul eléctrico o azul marino, tejido deportivo sencillo, cintura elástica), pies descalzos. Sin joyería. Aspecto genuinamente doméstico y sin artificio, apto para escenas nocturnas en su habitación. Fotografía de casting de cuerpo entero, estética cinematográfica fría y realista, grano fotográfico sutil, sin texto, sin logos, sin marcas visibles.

Prompt 4: Create the pink T-shirt look

viste a @img1 como Director de casting cinematográfico, fondo de estudio neutro gris azulado, luz plana y fría. Misma Luca (mullet ondulado con parte interna rubia, flequillo recto y corto, complexión gorda, piel pálida con pecas). De pie, cuerpo entero, mirada directa a cámara, postura relajada y natural. Viste camiseta de manga corta oversize en color rosa pastel lavado, silueta ancha y caída, cuello redondo sencillo (sin gráficos ni texto), combinada con pantalón vaquero ancho de pierna recta en tono verde-caqui envejecido con lavado desgastado (sin bordados ni parches decorativos visibles, denim liso), bota o zapatilla marrón sencilla asomando por debajo del bajo ancho del pantalón. Como accesorio, una horquilla pequeña en forma de estrella de color amarillo sujeta el flequillo o un mechón lateral del pelo, aportando un toque desenfadado e infantil-adolescente al conjunto. Sin joyería adicional. Estética de streetwear ancho y desestructurado, silueta oversize arriba y abajo. Fotografía de casting de cuerpo entero, estética cinematográfica fría y realista, grano fotográfico sutil, sin texto, sin logos, sin marcas visibles.

Prompt 5: Create the corset and cardigan look

viste a @img1 como **LOOK DE INSTITUTO (día a día)**
Director de casting cinematográfico, fondo de estudio neutro gris azulado, luz plana y fría. Misma Luca (mullet ondulado con parte interna rubia, flequillo recto y corto, complexión gorda, piel pálida con pecas). De pie, cuerpo entero, mirada directa a cámara, postura relajada. Viste top corsé sencillo en tono crudo/blanco roto con cordón fino ajustable en el escote, cárdigan o camisa holgada en gris oscuro colocada como capa suelta sobre los hombros (sin brillo satinado, versión de tela mate y cotidiana), pantalón ancho tipo "wide leg" en gris oscuro/antracita con bajo doblado, collar de cadena fina dorada sencillo, zapato plano blanco sencillo. Estilo desestructurado y con carácter, versión asequible/cotidiana del look de alfombra roja, no de gala. Fotografía de casting de cuerpo entero, estética cinematográfica fría y realista, grano fotográfico sutil, sin texto, sin logos, sin marcas visibles.

Prompt 6: Create the green cardigan look

viste a @img1 como **LOOK DE INSTITUTO (día a día)**
Director de casting cinematográfico, fondo de estudio neutro gris azulado, luz plana y fría. Misma Luca. De pie, cuerpo entero, mirada directa a cámara, postura neutra. Viste cárdigan de punto grueso en verde oliva desgastado sobre camiseta de banda vintage descolorida, pantalón vaquero ancho recto en azul oscuro, botas negras tipo combat boots con plataforma. Sin joyería llamativa. Estilo cotidiano de calle, apto para escenas de pasillo del instituto o llegada a clase. Fotografía de casting de cuerpo entero, estética cinematográfica fría y realista, grano fotográfico sutil, sin texto, sin logos, sin marcas visibles.

2. Build location references that stay consistent across scenes

Luca’s bedroom is both a setting and a way to show time passing. Its core elements remain recognizable: dark wooden furniture, a blue-green bedspread, a corkboard, a desk, and a mustard-colored lamp.

Lighting, clothing, and scattered objects change around that structure. A tidy room in daylight becomes a messier space during late-night rehearsals.

For your own film, approve the room layout before creating variations. Reuse that reference and check the position of the window, bed, desk, and shelves. Establishing the location early gives you a clearer visual target when generating the next shot.

Prompt 7: Establish the bedroom

Fotografía medio formato con grano: plano general completo de un dormitorio adolescente, sin marco de puerta en primer plano, encuadre amplio que muestra toda la estancia. Cama con colcha de punto en tono verde azulado apagado, almohadas variadas incluyendo una peluda en turquesa y otra con estampado de lunares, cabecero sencillo de madera oscura. Mesita de noche de madera con una lámpara de tulipa color mostaza encendida (única fuente de luz cálida en la habitación), una taza y objetos personales pequeños desordenados. Escritorio de madera oscura visible en la habitación, con superficie algo desordenada: papeles sueltos, algún libro abierto, un pequeño flexo apagado, silla sencilla de madera o metal. Pared con un panel de corcho hexagonal y varias fotos polaroid y recortes personales pinchados sin orden aparente, un pequeño póster o dibujo simple pegado en la pared. Estantería/cómoda baja de madera oscura con libros y objetos apilados sin mucho orden. Ventana con cortina fina de tela clara dejando entrar luz natural fría del exterior, guirnalda de lucecitas pequeñas colgando del techo cerca del techo, apagadas o muy tenues. Ambiente íntimo, algo desordenado pero acogedor, luz general fría y tenue con solo el cálido punto de la lámpara de mesa como contraste, atmósfera contemplativa y solitaria. Estética cinematográfica realista, grano fotográfico sutil, colores desaturados con dominante azul-verdosa en las sombras y un único acento cálido en la fuente de luz práctica, sin texto, sin logos, sin marcas visibles.

Prompt 8: Bedroom variation: unmade bed

**CAMA DESHECHA**
Fotografía medio formato con grano, plano general fijo de la habitación desde la esquina, encuadre en diagonal: a la izquierda una estantería baja de madera oscura con libros y objetos personales fijos, y un panel de corcho con las mismas fotos polaroid, notas y un póster pequeño en la pared (elementos constantes). En el centro, una cama de madera oscura con cabecero de listones, colcha de punto azul verdoso completamente deshecha y arrugada, sábanas revueltas, cojines (gris, peludo turquesa, de lunares) caídos y desordenados. A la derecha, una mesita de noche con lámpara de cerámica y pantalla mostaza encendida, sobre ella solo un vaso de agua y el móvil bocabajo. Al fondo a la derecha, un escritorio de madera oscura con silla, vacío de actividad reciente, solo un par de libros de texto cerrados y un bote de lápices. Al fondo, ventana con cortina fina blanca y guirnalda de luces con bombillas apagada. Luz cálida de la lámpara de mesa como fuente principal, resto en penumbra fría azulada, estética cinematográfica realista, grano fotográfico sutil, sin texto, sin logos, sin marcas visibles.

Prompt 9: Bedroom variation: clothes on the bed

**ROPA EN LA CAMA**
Fotografía medio formato con grano, mismo plano general fijo de la habitación desde la esquina, misma composición diagonal, estantería y panel de corcho con las mismas fotos y póster a la izquierda (elementos constantes). Cama de madera oscura en el centro con la colcha azul verdosa parcialmente cubierta de ropa desordenada (camisetas, un cárdigan de punto, una falda de cuadros tartán, calcetines sueltos), cojines empujados hacia un lado. Mesita de noche a la derecha con lámpara mostaza encendida, sobre ella un espejo de mano pequeño y un par de pendientes sueltos. Escritorio al fondo a la derecha con la silla apartada, superficie con una revista abierta y un neceser de maquillaje entreabierto. Ventana al fondo con cortina fina y guirnalda de luces apagada (luz de tarde). Ambiente habitado y personal, luz cálida de la lámpara contrastando con el resto en penumbra, estética cinematográfica realista, grano fotográfico sutil, sin texto, sin logos, sin marcas visibles.

Prompt 10: Bedroom variation: daytime

**DE DÍA**
Fotografía medio formato con grano, mismo plano general fijo de la habitación desde la esquina, misma composición diagonal: estantería y panel de corcho con las mismas fotos y póster a la izquierda (elementos constantes), cama de madera oscura en el centro con colcha azul verdosa bien hecha y cojines colocados. Mesita de noche a la derecha con la lámpara apagada, sobre ella un despertador y una planta pequeña en maceta. Escritorio al fondo a la derecha con la silla colocada, superficie ordenada: una mochila apoyada contra la pata de la mesa y un cuaderno cerrado. Luz natural fría entrando por la ventana del fondo a través de la cortina fina blanca, guirnalda de luces apagada de día, iluminación general difusa y plana. Ambiente ordenado y tranquilo, tonos azul-grisáceos desaturados, estética cinematográfica realista, grano fotográfico sutil, sin texto, sin logos, sin marcas visibles.

Prompt 11: Bedroom variation: nighttime rehearsal

**NOCHE DE ENSAYO (escritorio en uso)**
Fotografía medio formato con grano, mismo plano general fijo de la habitación desde la esquina, misma composición diagonal, estantería y panel de corcho con las mismas fotos y póster a la izquierda (elementos constantes). Escena nocturna: la lámpara de la mesita encendida junto con un flexo de escritorio también encendido a la derecha, iluminando papeles con anotaciones y tachones esparcidos sobre la mesa (letra de una canción escrita a mano), un móvil apoyado en pie contra unos libros como si grabara, silla del escritorio ligeramente girada. Mesita de noche con solo la lámpara y un vaso de agua. Cama con la colcha azul verdosa sin hacer del todo. Ventana al fondo oscura con la guirnalda de luces encendida tenuemente. Dos fuentes de luz cálida puntual (lámpara de mesita y flexo del escritorio) contra el resto de la habitación en sombras frías, ambiente de concentración nocturna, estética cinematográfica realista, grano fotográfico marcado, sin texto, sin logos, sin marcas visibles.

Prompt 12: Bedroom variation: night

**DE NOCHE**
Fotografía medio formato con grano, mismo plano general fijo de la habitación desde la esquina, misma composición diagonal, estantería y panel de corcho con las mismas fotos y póster a la izquierda (elementos constantes). Ventana al fondo completamente oscura, cortina fina apenas visible, guirnalda de luces con bombillas encendida sobre la ventana. Cama en el centro con la colcha azul verdosa colocada pero algo removida, como recién usada. Mesita de noche a la derecha con la lámpara mostaza encendida como fuente principal, sobre ella unos auriculares y un vaso vacío. Escritorio al fondo a la derecha en penumbra, silla vacía, superficie casi despejada salvo una lámpara de escritorio apagada. Ambiente íntimo y solitario, alto contraste entre luz cálida puntual y sombras frías, estética cinematográfica realista, grano fotográfico marcado, sin texto, sin logos, sin marcas visibles.

3. Design recurring props before generating the action

The audition introduces a different visual world: a red backdrop, reflective stage floor, judges’ table, and the illuminated “THE SPOTLIGHT” sign. Harder, warmer lighting shifts the mood from private rehearsal to public exposure.

The flyer connects those two worlds. It appears in the bedroom and returns as Luca approaches the audition, so its design needs to remain recognizable.

For Out Loud, the flyer began with a Magnific stock template, edited in Designer. Prepare your final wording, colors, and layout before using a graphic as a video reference. For details that need exact lettering, plan the finished graphic in advance and composite it in post where needed.

Establish the relationship between the venue’s exterior and interior, too. Choose references that feel like parts of the same building and production.

Prompt 13: Establish the talent-show studio

Fotógrafo profesional de localizaciones cinematográficas en 2026, ambientación británica de 2010: interior de un plató de televisión profesional de tamaño medio, con aspecto de producción televisiva establecida (no un centro cívico reconvertido, sino un estudio de grabación real), visto desde el fondo de la zona de público. Estructura de trusses metálicos de gran escala con múltiples focos de teatro y paneles LED colgados en lo alto, iluminación escénica compleja y bien resuelta con varios haces de luz dura y algo de humo/haze atmosférico controlado. Al fondo, un panel decorativo de fondo de mayor producción con el rótulo "THE SPOTLIGHT" en formato marquesina iluminada con bombillas @Flyer , acabado pulido y profesional propio de una cadena nacional de televisión de la época, con calidad de diseño alta aunque manteniendo la estética británica de 2010. Delante del escenario, una mesa de jueces con acabado elegante (superficie lacada o cristal, iluminación de acento integrada). Los tres jueces @JURADO_1  @JURADO_2  @JURADO_3  sentados a la mesa están de espaldas a la cámara/público, mirando hacia el escenario vacío frente a ellos, donde se colocará el participante. 5. Adapt the prompts to your own shot list

Use these prompts as a starting point for your own direction. Before generating, make sure each shot gives a clear instruction for the result you want.

  • Make text exceptions explicit. If you need a sign or number, distinguish it from instructions that exclude other text. Use a blank surface when adding the design in post.
  • Match references to the scene. Check that the attached image has the intended outfit, room state, and lighting, even when an asset’s name suggests something different.
  • Clarify the shot list. The rehearsal block includes shared setup directions before its performance shots. List the shots you want explicitly when adapting it.
  • Replace incomplete reference labels. Some original bedroom names end in an ellipsis. Link your complete, approved references.
  • Keep timing flexible. Split longer sequences into smaller groups when needed, then refine their pace in the edit.

The goal is to give each generation a clear visual and dramatic purpose. Review it against that purpose before deciding what to change.

6. Bring the film together in post-production

After video generation, Out Loud moved through HD conversion in Magnific, post-production in After Effects, and editing in Premiere Pro.

This is where individual performances become a sequence. A glance needs enough time to register. A reaction shot needs to arrive at the right moment. A pause can give the audience room to understand what Luca is experiencing.

Use post-production to make recurring text and graphic elements consistent, including participant numbers and event signage. Shape the music, dialogue, and ambient sound around the emotional rhythm of your cut.

Before export, review the film for character continuity, wardrobe, room layout, props, stage geography, and crop. Watch it once without sound to check whether the gestures and reactions communicate on their own.

Build your next AI film around clear creative decisions

Out Loud brings character design, location development, performance direction, and editing into one filmmaking process. Each reference establishes something the next scene can build on. Each prompt describes a moment that earns its place in the story.

Start with a character and one environment. Develop a short sequence, review what stays consistent, and refine the action before moving on. Use the prompts above to explore how framing, lighting, and small gestures can support your own story.

3D figurines in 2026 span a longer chain than most people expect when they tap "generate." A collectible on your desk might start as concept art, become a triangle mesh, survive Blender cleanup, slice for resin or FDM, and end in a product photo for Shopify. AI shortcuts the middle steps, but it does not erase them.

The hard part is not the first cute render. It is wall thickness for printing, support strategy under chins and capes, scale when a 32 mm tabletop mini shares a build plate with a 6-inch display piece, and likeness when the figurine is supposed to be a specific person.

Magnific owns the upstream lane: character concept art, orthographic reference sheets, upscaled textures, packaging mockups, and team review before any mesher touches the file.

Concept art, printable meshes, and finished prints: three stages

Stage one is look development. You lock silhouette, costume, and paint scheme in 2D. Magnific image generation with reference images and Custom Characters keeps the same hero readable across front, side, and three-quarter views sculptors expect.

Stage two is mesh generation. Meshy, Tripo3D, and Kaedim lift concept renders into GLB or OBJ files. Single-image lifts guess hidden sides. Multi-view orthographic uploads produce stabler miniatures when you invest in Stage one.

Stage three is fabrication. Blender repairs non-manifold edges, adds print bases, and exports STL. Shapeways or your bench printer turns resin into object. Polycam enters when you scan a clay sculpt or an existing figurine to digitize instead of generating from scratch.

Our image to 3D model guide goes deeper on photogrammetry when the source is a real object, not a painting. Our AI 3D model generation guide compares text-to-mesh engines when you skip photography entirely. Viral blister-pack 2D toy art lives in our AI action figure generator article when marketing needs shelf photography before plastic exists.

Best 8 tools for 3D figurines in every workflow in 2026

1. Magnific

Magnific is not a slicer and does not ship STL files from a single button. It is the art direction hub that makes downstream meshes less embarrassing.

Strength is beat markers, lyric captions, and mobile export to TikTok and Reels. AI video adds template effects and filters. Assembly runs on a full timeline. Free tier with optional Pro. Best for final sync and social delivery after clips are generated elsewhere.

5. Suno

Suno leads many artists' music-first pipeline: generate full songs with vocals from prompts, then build visuals elsewhere. Suno is not a replacement for a timeline editor, but pairing Suno masters with Magnific video clips is a common 2026 workflow for unsigned acts without a label budget.

Check Suno and your distributor's terms before commercial release of AI vocals.

Strength is full song generation with vocals from prompts. Video must pair with external tools. Exports are audio masters. Free tier and paid plans available. Best for demo tracks that need visuals fast when the music lane leads the pipeline.

For deeper music-model comparison, see our AI song generator guide.

6. Pika

Pika optimizes punchy 6-second hooks: melt effects, inflate, Pikaframes transitions between two stills. Music videos need dozens of hooks for TikTok; Pika's iteration speed beats cinematic tools when the goal is A/B testing chorus drops.

Physics ceiling is lower than Runway for complex dance environments. Use Pika for hooks, Magnific or Runway for hero verses.

Strength is fast stylized loops for chorus-drop teasers. No built-in music suite. Exports are short MP4 clips. Subscription tiers apply. Best for TikTok hooks and A/B testing chorus drops before the full MV lands.

7. Luma Dream Machine

Luma Dream Machine delivers smooth camera moves and coherent scene extension from still key art. Artists with strong cover photography can animate album art into drifting B-roll for lyric sections.

No native lip sync or music timeline. Pair with Magnific Lip Sync or CapCut assembly.

Strength is cinematic B-roll from still key art with smooth camera moves. Assembly means exporting clips out to a timeline editor. Free tier and paid plans exist. Best for lyric-section atmosphere when album art should drift into motion.

8. DomoAI

DomoAI targets anime and stylized transformation: turn live footage into anime motion or apply preset styles that match VTuber and J-pop aesthetics. Fits our AI anime generator lane when the MV must look like a series opening.

Character consistency across a full three-minute cut still needs planning and reference discipline.

Strength is anime and style-transfer MVs from video or image uploads. Assembly exports individual clips for external timelines. Credit-based pricing. Best for anime-style and VTuber promos that match series-opening aesthetics.

How these 8 AI music video generators compare

Use Magnific for the full promo pipeline with Music Generator plus Voice, beat-sync assembly in Video Project Editor, Lip Sync in Clip Editor, and multi-shot in Video Generator. Runway fits cinematic performance with Act Two lip sync but external music and NLE assembly. Kaiber fits abstract reactive MVs with uploaded tracks and in-app reactive assembly. CapCut fits final edit and social with strong beat markers and caption templates. Suno fits AI vocal masters with native songs but no video timeline. Pika fits short hooks via Pikaframes with limited lip sync. Luma fits B-roll from stills with scene extension but external assembly. DomoAI fits anime MVs with style presets and limited lip sync.

Official Magnific workflow: track to finished MV

This sequence mirrors Magnific documentation across Audio tools, Video Generator, Clip Editor, and Video Project Editor.

Step 1: Lock or generate audio. If you need an original track, open the Music Generator. Prompt with genre, mood, tempo, and vocal intent per Magnific docs (producer-brief structure). Download the master or keep it in Creations. If you already have a WAV or MP3, skip to Step 2.

Step 2: Plan shots. Mark bar numbers for intro, verse, chorus, and bridge on your waveform in any DAW or CapCut. Decide which sections need performance (Lip Sync) versus abstract B-roll (image-to-video).

Step 3: Generate clips. Open the AI Video Generator. For narrative sections, use Multi-shot on Wan, Kling 3.0, or Seedance with one prompt per shot. For performance, generate a character still with Custom Characters, then image-to-video with motion prompts. For temp synced sound in one pass, pick a native audio model and include audio cues in the prompt per Magnific docs.

Step 4: Polish in Clip Editor. Apply Color Grading LUTs (see our AI filter guide for look-development context). Run Lip Sync on performance clips with your vocal stem. Add Motion Shake on chorus hits if needed. Upscale last.

Step 5: Assemble. Open the Video Project Editor. Import clips from History. Add the master track on the audio lane (upload MP3/WAV or Use from Creations). Trim clip edges to downbeats. Add cut or fade transitions. Match audio and video end points per Magnific docs.

Step 6: Export and archive. Export at target resolution. Credit cost displays before confirm. Store variant cuts in Spaces for label review.

Music video shot checklist

Use this block when briefing models or your editor:

  • Aspect ratio: 9:16 for TikTok/Reels hooks, 16:9 for YouTube master (generate both branches in Spaces)
  • Hook first: 3-second visual punch before bar one for scroll-stopping feeds
  • Verse vs chorus: slower camera on verses, faster cuts or shake on chorus per Clip Editor Motion Shake
  • Performance vs B-roll: tag clips so Lip Sync runs only on face-forward takes
  • Lyric alignment: caption templates in CapCut or Magnific exports with burned-in text only when labels approve
  • Palette lock: Custom Styles in image generation before video to keep album art colors consistent
  • Duration math: count clips needed (e.g., twelve 8-second gens cover 96 seconds before trims)
  • Stem exports: keep instrumental and vocal stems for cleaner Lip Sync input

Artist promos, lyric visuals, and social hooks

Unsigned artist drop Suno or Magnific Music Generator for the track, Magnific multi-shot for verse storyboards, CapCut for final bar snaps and captions.

Label lyric video Luma B-roll from approved stills, Magnific assembly with label-provided master, no Lip Sync unless talent cleared likeness.

Dance challenge Runway Act Two or Kaiber reactive styles for body motion, export 9:16 hooks from Pika for challenge templates.

Anime OP aesthetic DomoAI style pass plus Magnific color LUTs for broadcast-style grades.

Background swaps on performance footage when location changes mid-song, use Clip Editor Modify prompts or image background tools before reassembling on the timeline.

Seven mistakes that break beat sync

  1. Generating one long clip. Models cap duration; plan sequences instead.
  2. Lip Sync on wrong stem. Use isolated vocals via Audio Isolation when the mix is dense.
  3. Upscaling before edits. Magnific docs recommend upscale last to save credits.
  4. Ignoring audio length mismatch. Trim master and picture to the same end frame in the Video Project Editor.
  5. Random aspect ratios. Mixing 1:1 and 9:16 in one timeline without reframing.
  6. No shot list per section. Chorus and verse need different motion energy.
  7. Publishing uncleared samples. AI music tools do not grant third-party sample rights.

Sync rights, samples, and commercial use

Magnific states AI-generated video and audio are subject to Magnific Terms and Conditions for AI Products. Commercial use requires compliance with those terms and avoidance of infringing third-party IP.

Master recording rights belong to whoever owns the song. AI-generated vocals from Suno or Magnific Music Generator still need clearance for commercial distribution on streaming platforms.

Sync license connecting music to video is separate from the generative tool license. Labels expect paperwork even when visuals are AI.

Likeness Lip Sync on a real artist face without consent creates publicity risk. Use fictional characters or cleared talent.

Training data concerns Some distributors flag fully AI vocal releases. Check your platform's 2026 policy before upload day.

What is the best AI music video generator in 2026?

Magnific fits teams that need music, video generation, lip sync, and timeline export in one suite. Kaiber fits abstract audio-reactive visuals. CapCut fits final beat sync and social captions.

Can AI sync video to my song automatically?

Full three-minute auto-sync is still rare. Native audio models generate temp synced sound in one pass. For your master track, use timeline assembly in Magnific Video Project Editor or CapCut beat markers.

How do I add lip sync to a music video?

Magnific documents Lip Sync in the Clip Editor: upload a performance clip, provide vocal audio or generated voice, and generate synced mouth movement. Use isolated vocal stems for best results.

Magnific docs list Multi-shot on Wan 2.5/2.6, Kling 3.0, Kling 3.0 Omni, Seedance 1.5 Pro, and Seedance 2.0 with up to six shots per generation.

Can I use AI music videos on YouTube and Spotify?

Tool terms allow personal and professional use when you follow Magnific Terms of Use. Streaming platforms add their own rules for AI vocals and samples. Confirm distributor policy before monetizing.

Should I generate music and video in the same tool?

Not required. Many artists use Suno or Magnific Music Generator for audio and Magnific Video Generator for visuals, then assemble in the Video Project Editor. One platform reduces export and format friction.

  2. LALAL.AI

  7. Adobe Audition
  8. BandLab Splitter

Methodology: this ranking compares documented features and workflow fit. We did not run a controlled hands-on test. Product details were checked on 2026-09-21; verify current plans and limits before choosing.

An AI stem splitter separates a mixed song or clip into isolated parts: vocals, drums, bass, instruments, or noise-reduced dialogue. DJs want acapellas. Producers want stems for remixes. Video editors want clean voice tracks for Lip Sync without the music bed fighting the model.

In 2026, quality still hinges on source format, how dense the original mix is, and whether you need four stems or just the vocal line for one scene.

Magnific documents Audio Isolation in Clip Editor for speech, music, and background components on video clips, plus Voice Generator, Music Generator, and Video Project Editor assembly when you replace stems inside a full audiovisual project. Dedicated stem apps still win on multi-track music exports.

Vocal isolation, full stems, and video audio lanes

Two-stem vocal removers output vocals plus everything else (or instrumental minus vocal). Fast for karaoke and sample pulls.

Multi-stem engines split drums, bass, piano, guitar, and other layers. Better for remix sessions where you mute one instrument without killing the whole backing track.

Video audio isolation targets dialogue, music, and ambience inside a clip without exporting a full song project. Magnific Clip Editor Audio Isolation fits Lip Sync prep and dialogue cleanup on generated or filmed footage.

Music-first workflows overlap with our AI song generator guide when you generate replacement beds instead of reusing copyrighted masters. Beat-sync video projects overlap with our AI music video generator guide when isolated vocals feed Lip Sync on performance clips.

Best 8 AI stem splitters for every audio workflow in 2026

1. Magnific

Magnific is the platform pick when stem work sits inside a video or marketing pipeline, not a DAW-only remix session.

Magnific Clip Editor documents Audio Isolation: upload or open a clip with audio, choose which components to keep or remove (speech, music, background noise), and generate a version suited to Lip Sync, cleaner voiceover, or music-only exports. Access via the Clip Editor at magnific.com/pikaso/video-clip-editor after generation or from Creations.

That is different from a four-stem music splitter. It is optimized for post clips where you need one clean lane fast. Pair isolated dialogue with Magnific Lip Sync, drop a new bed from the Music Generator at magnific.com/pikaso/music, or re-voice lines with the Voice Generator. Assemble final mixes in the Video Project Editor on the audio track.

Spaces stores version branches when legal wants dialogue-only cuts separate from music-forward social exports. Broader clip polish (grade, stabilize, Modify) lives in the same Clip Editor docs referenced in our video background changer guide.

Magnific does not replace LALAL.AI for producer-grade four-stem WAV exports from a mastered stereo file. It wins when the deliverable is MP4 with cleaner audio, not a remix ZIP for Ableton.

2. LALAL.AI

LALAL.AI is the default name producers cite for AI stem separation. Upload a stereo mix, pick vocal, instrumental, drums, bass, piano, or other stem types depending on tier, and download high-quality WAV outputs.

Processing is cloud-based with per-minute pricing on paid plans. Isolation quality on modern pop and hip-hop is strong, though bleeding can remain on heavily distorted guitars or dense choral stacks. Best when the job is music stems and you already have a finished master file.

3. Moises

Moises targets musicians and practice workflows: isolate vocals, split stems, change song key and tempo, and jam along with muted drums or bass in the mobile app.

The UX favors gigging players and content creators who want stems on a phone between sets. Export formats and batch controls are lighter than desktop DAW pipelines, but speed and chord detection keep it on many shortlists.

4. RipX

RipX (Hit'n'Mix) goes deeper than simple stem buttons. It visualizes notes inside mixed audio so you can edit individual pitched content after separation.

The learning curve is real. Reward is surgical control when a remix needs one keyboard line changed without re-exporting the whole instrumental from another tool.

5. iZotope RX

iZotope RX is the broadcast and post-production standard for isolating dialogue, removing bleed, and cleaning problematic recordings. Music stem separation exists in the ecosystem, but RX shines on dialogue rescue and forensic cleanup.

Price and depth target professionals. Casual karaoke users should start with Moises or LALAL.AI instead.

6. Ultimate Vocal Remover

Ultimate Vocal Remover (UVR) is the free open-source desktop stack many producers run locally with Demucs and other models. No subscription, full control over model choice, and offline privacy for unreleased tracks.

Setup takes more effort than a web upload button. CPU and GPU time scales with song length. Ideal for hobbyists and engineers who batch stems overnight.

7. Adobe Audition

Adobe Audition bundles spectral editing, AI repair effects, and stem-style separation inside Creative Cloud. Teams already cutting in Premiere use Audition to pull cleaner VO from messy location audio before picture lock.

It is not the fastest dedicated stem SaaS. Integration with Premiere and Photoshop-heavy marketing pipelines keeps it on agency tool lists.

8. BandLab Splitter

BandLab Splitter offers free browser-based stem separation for vocals, drums, bass, and other parts with a low-friction upload flow. Good first test when you want to hear whether a track separates cleanly before you spend credits elsewhere.

Advanced remix editing and video assembly happen outside BandLab. Export stems and continue in your DAW or Magnific video timeline.

How these 8 AI stem splitters compare

Use Magnific when stems support video Lip Sync, dialogue cleanup, and full clip export in one Creative Suite. LALAL.AI and Moises lead music stem downloads for remix and practice. RipX fits note-level editing after separation. iZotope RX fits dialogue and forensic repair. UVR fits free local batch processing. Adobe Audition fits Premiere-linked post. BandLab Splitter fits quick free browser tests.

If you only need an instrumental for a cover video, a two-stem pass is enough. If you are remixing for release, export WAV stems from LALAL.AI or UVR and mix in a DAW. If you are fixing AI-generated performance clips, start with Magnific Audio Isolation before Lip Sync.

Magnific workflow: isolate, replace, and publish

Open your clip in Clip Editor from Creations or after AI video generation. Run Audio Isolation and keep speech while removing music if Lip Sync struggles on dense mixes.

Generate replacement music in Music Generator or upload a licensed instrumental. Place isolated or new audio on the Video Project Editor timeline and trim to match picture.

Archive dialogue-only and full-mix exports as separate branches in Spaces for client review.

Lyric-led replacements can start from our song lyrics generator workflow before you record new vocals in Voice Generator.

Before you split: source file checklist

  • Use lossless or high-bitrate sources when possible. WAV or FLAC masters separate cleaner than 128 kbps MP3 rips.
  • Confirm you have rights to process the file. Splitting copyrighted music for commercial remix still needs clearance.
  • Match project sample rate. Export stems at the same rate as your session (commonly 44.1 kHz or 48 kHz).
  • Label exports immediately. Name files with song title, stem type, and date so DAW imports do not overwrite each other.
  • Keep the original mix. Archive the stereo master before destructive edits.
  • For video clips, trim handles. Isolate only the section you need to save credits and processing time.
  • Check phase after recombination. Preview vocal plus instrumental before you publish in case isolation introduced artifacts.

Common stem splitting mistakes

  • Expecting perfect silence on instrumentals. Vocal remover artifacts often sound like underwater reverb on cymbals. Audition before release.
  • Splitting already compressed social audio. Ripped TikTok audio rarely yields pro stems.
  • Using music stems for Lip Sync without checking bleed. Run Magnific Audio Isolation on the video clip instead of a guessed acapella export.
  • Ignoring stereo phase. Summing stems incorrectly can hollow out the mix.
  • Wrong stem count for the job. Do not buy four-stem exports when you only needed vocals.
  • Publishing karaoke of major label tracks. Platform policy and copyright still apply.
  • Skipping level matching. Re-imported stems may need gain adjustment before mastering.

Karaoke, remixes, and cleaner video dialogue

  • Karaoke and cover videos: LALAL.AI or Moises for instrumentals, Magnific for final video assembly and captions.
  • Remix and sample chops: UVR or LALAL.AI stems into Ableton or Logic, RipX for note edits.
  • Podcast and interview cleanup: iZotope RX or Magnific Audio Isolation on clip audio.
  • AI music video Lip Sync: Magnific isolation on performance clips per our AI music video generator guide.
  • Social hooks without licensed masters: Magnific Music Generator beds instead of splitting commercial radio tracks.
  • Animated explainers: Voice Generator narration plus isolated SFX from Magnific audio tools in our [animated video maker](https://www.magnific.com/blog/animated-video-maker/) pipeline.

Copyright and commercial use

Magnific AI audio is subject to Magnific Terms and Conditions for AI Products. Stem separation does not grant remix rights to the underlying song. Commercial releases need permission from rights holders unless you own the master.

Isolated vocals from celebrity tracks do not clear sampling rules for sold beats. AI-generated replacement music from Magnific Music Generator follows Magnific tool terms but still needs human review for unintended resemblance to existing works.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best AI stem splitter in 2026?

LALAL.AI and Moises lead music stem exports. Magnific leads video workflows with Clip Editor Audio Isolation plus Lip Sync and timeline assembly. UVR leads free local processing.

Can Magnific split song stems like a DAW tool?

Magnific documents Audio Isolation on video clips (speech, music, background), not full four-stem music exports from stereo masters. Use LALAL.AI or UVR for that lane.

How do I isolate vocals for karaoke?

Upload the track to LALAL.AI, Moises, or BandLab Splitter, download the instrumental, and sing over the export. Check licensing before public performance or monetized video.

What file format should stems be?

WAV is safest for production. MP3 stems add compression artifacts that stack when you remix.

Why does my instrumental still have ghost vocals?

Dense harmonies, reverb-heavy vocals, and low-quality sources leave bleed. Try a different model in UVR or accept manual EQ/notch cleanup in a DAW.

Is stem splitting legal?

Personal practice is common, but commercial remix, distribution, and monetized covers require rights to the original composition and master recording.
